name: rules

name: hooks

name: doctor

name: trust
description: Whether this project is trusted, and what that covers: /trust [yes|no]

name: forget-approvals
description: Forget every remembered approval and every rule added in this session

name: account

name: advise
description: Ask the advisor, a second model, about the work so far; only you see the answer [question]

name: agents
description: The agents of this session and the definitions they can be started from

name: allow-edit
description: Let the next edit of a file through, whatever the agent has read of it <path>

name: bg
description: Run a prompt in the background, in a copy of this session <prompt>

name: coordinator
description: Have the lead only plan and delegate: it keeps no tool that edits or runs commands on | off | status

name: ext
description: List the loaded extensions and Luau scripts, with the errors of disabled scripts

name: fast

name: goal
description: Set an objective the agent works on until it is verified <objective> | status | pause | resume | drop

name: login

name: logout

name: lsp
description: Language servers and their state

name: review

description: Have a reviewer look for security defects in the same changes [ref]

name: settings
description: Sign in, add API keys, choose models and change every setting

name: skills
description: List skills and where they come from

name: slow
description: Cheaper, slower replies (the economy tier) [on|off|status]

name: stats
description: Tokens and cost per day, provider, model, project and agent, from the usage log [days]

name: stop
description: Stop an agent and the agents it started <agent id|all>

name: task
description: Start an agent yourself; its report goes to the lead <agent> [name=<id>] <prompt>

name: usage

name: verify
description: Run the project's checks and a verifier agent on the work so far [what should be true]

name: skill:api-design
description: Use when designing or reviewing an interface other programs call: an HTTP or RPC API, a library's public surface, or a wire format. Covers resource and RPC conventions, errors, pagination, idempotency and versioning.

name: skill:azazel-extensions
description: Use when customising this harness: writing a Luau extension (tools, event handlers, commands), configuring hooks, defining a custom agent, adding a slash command, or writing a skill. Contains the file locations, formats and API tables for each.

name: skill:browser-testing
description: Use to check a web page or web app in a real browser with the browser tool: confirming a change works, walking a user flow, finding why a page is broken, or capturing evidence. Snapshot, act, assert, with console and network checks.

name: skill:code-review
description: Use to review a change (a diff, a branch, a pull request, or work another agent just finished) before it is accepted. Gives a rubric, severity levels and a findings format that separates defects from preferences.

name: skill:debugging
description: Use when something fails, crashes, hangs or gives a wrong result and the cause is not yet known. A disciplined loop of reproduce, isolate, hypothesise, instrument, fix and prove, including bisection across history and inputs.

name: skill:design-tokens
description: Use when starting a project's visual system or replacing scattered values with one: derives colour, type, spacing, radius and shadow tokens from a brief or an existing brand colour and emits them as CSS variables and a Tailwind theme.

name: skill:docs-writing
description: Use when writing or restructuring documentation: a README, a getting-started tutorial, a how-to guide, reference pages or a changelog. Gives the structure for each kind and the checks that keep documentation true.

name: skill:frontend-design
description: Use when building or restyling a user interface (a page, a component, a whole app) and the result has to look designed rather than generated. Covers hierarchy, type, spacing, colour, states, responsive behaviour and motion, and how to check the work in a real browser.

name: skill:game-dev
description: Use when working on a game project in Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, Roblox or Bevy: finding your way around the project, following the engine's conventions, producing and importing assets with the generate tools and sprite_sheet, and building, running and playtesting from the command line.

name: skill:git-workflow
description: Use when the task involves git beyond a simple status or diff: shaping commits, working on branches, resolving merge or rebase conflicts, finding the commit that introduced a bug, recovering lost work, or using worktrees. Sub-agents never push; the lead pushes only when the user asks.

name: skill:mcp-builder
description: Use when writing, extending or debugging a Model Context Protocol server so that agents can use a service, a data source or a local program as tools. Covers tool design, the stdio and HTTP transports, and testing the server against this harness.

name: skill:media-generation
description: Use when producing images, video, 3D models or audio with the generate tools, or sprite sheets from generated frames. Prompt patterns for each kind, how to keep a set of assets in one style, and how to check results before using them.

name: skill:performance
description: Use when something is too slow or uses too much memory, or before optimising anything. Measure first, find the bottleneck with the right profiler for the ecosystem, change one thing, and prove the gain with a benchmark.

name: skill:playtest
description: Use to run a game or application build and try it the way a player or user would: launching it, operating it through screen capture and input (or the browser for web builds), and reporting defects with the frames that show them.

name: skill:refactoring
description: Use when restructuring code without changing what it does: extracting, renaming, moving, splitting modules, replacing a pattern across a codebase, or cleaning up before a feature. Characterisation tests first, then small mechanical steps that each keep the build green.

name: skill:release-engineering
description: Use when preparing a release or the machinery around one: choosing a version number, writing a changelog, setting up CI build and test matrices, cross-compiling, and packaging binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux. Publishing itself stays with the user.

name: skill:reverse-engineering
description: Use when the task is to understand software or data without its source: triaging an unknown binary, recovering behaviour and data structures in a disassembler, working out a file format or a network protocol, or finding what changed between two builds. For software you own or are authorised to analyse.

name: skill:security-review
description: Use to look for security defects in code you are allowed to assess: a change before merge, a feature that handles untrusted input, or a whole service. Covers injection, authorisation, secrets, deserialisation, request forgery to internal services, and dependency risk, with a findings format that requires evidence.

name: skill:testing
description: Use when writing or extending tests, deciding what level a test belongs at, or dealing with flaky or slow tests. Covers choosing behaviours and boundaries, fixtures and test data, doubles, and making tests deterministic.

name: skill:ui-review
description: Use to audit an existing interface for accessibility and usability problems: contrast, keyboard and focus order, semantics and names, forms and error states, responsive behaviour. Produces a findings report with severity, evidence and a fix for each item.
